lens_summary: Lens: model retraining that can finish and be scored by 29 Sep 10:00 UTC. Honest verdict: no retrain in this window has evidence for a step change (>= +0.005). All the evidence points one way. Plain retrains of the pilkwang stack land at or below the public weights: leonixis 199-video/60-epoch = 0.947; Kai-Gowers 400-epoch DDP = 0.927 vs 0.942 shipped, with detector recall 96.7 vs 98.3 %; our fine-tunes 0.944/0.943 vs 0.947; our scratch secondary 0.920. The only retrained detector known to beat the wall (georgexue666/easonyanyan: pool-2, sigma 0.8 um, plus a retrained edge model) reached 0.950, i.e. +0.003. The x138 head's +0.007 was probably at most ~+0.004 of localisation, because the head also cut final nodes by 2.9 %: 0.1 x 0.029 x 0.91 = +0.0026 of node multiplier. The v2 dose-response puts the ceiling of removing the remaining grid quantisation at +0.001..+0.002. Sharper targets or full XY resolution therefore cannot be the lever. The big lab error classes, b_swap 2,175 FN and a_never 1,907 FN, are 4-10 um geometric offsets. Mostly along z, they are unlearnable from raw patches (|r| <= 0.09). In 44b6 they are partly under-segmentation of z-blurred neighbours. The one retraining mechanism aimed at that is a dense-label proposal detector, and it is sub-step and slow. What the lens can deliver: (1) a corrected, embryo-robust V1284 head. It trains in CPU-minutes from the existing 199-video capture. The old kill test used an embryo-IN-sample reference and was biased against it. Expected -0.002..+0.002, no GPU, one probe. (2) A proposal-only copy of the detector trained on dense Ultrack/dorado labels. Its peaks would feed only x138's low-detection pool (readmit/gapfill), leaving the UNet features, edge network and head untouched, which avoids the -0.038 frozen-linker trap. Expected 0..+0.003, needs friend A. (3) A training-free test of whether the hidden annotations follow Ultrack's segmentation convention, which would make an Ultrack-derived localiser embryo-invariant. (4) A joint fine-tune, the top-team lever, as a gated long shot. Lens ceiling by 29 Sep: about +0.003..+0.005 if everything works, expected ~+0.001. 0.99 is out of reach: the LB top is 0.975, and 0.99 would need adjusted edge J >= ~0.94-0.95 at division J 0.4-0.5. The top teams got there with weeks of embryo-held-out model iteration, not with a 4-day retrain.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: The 199-video head retrain failed because it learns the 6bba z offset, so the head line is closed (kill test FAIL).
challenged_assumptions.why_doubtful: The kill-test reference is wrong. x138's validator trained the public head on ~10 stems per embryo, so in each embryo-held-out fold the public head is IN-embryo. 44b6 clips are overlapping crops of one recording, so dropping the 10 probable train stems does not remove that leakage. The new head is out-of-embryo. The test compares an out-of-embryo head against an in-embryo head and cannot pass by design. Per-embryo debiasing (run Q) already cut the embryo shift gap from 0.588 um (P) to 0.212/0.071 um. Q beats 'none' by 8.1 % (44b6) and 7.7 % (6bba) fully out-of-embryo. The public head beats 'none' by 13.5 % and 8.9 % while in-embryo. The fair comparator is the x138 recipe retrained on 10 stems of the TRAINING embryo only.

hypotheses.title: V1284 head v2: debiased, embryo-balanced, bagged 199-video head with a corrected out-of-embryo gate (CPU-only retrain)
hypotheses.mechanism: The x138 head de-quantises peaks on the 1.625 um grid: mean shift 0.74 um, pooled mean distance 1.686 -> 1.525 um. It was trained on only 4,136 pairs from 20 movies, and x138's own note says volume was its limit (4 movies +14.9 % worse, 20 movies -10.4 %). We already hold a bit-exact 199-video capture: 125,700 pairs, 30 s CPU per fit. Its failure was a biased test, not a biased model. With per-embryo debias (Q), the embryo shift gap drops to 0.07-0.21 um, and it improves on 'none' by 7.7-8.1 % in both out-of-embryo directions. The remaining risk on unseen embryos is the annotation convention, which differs by embryo (none-bias z +0.18 um on 44b6 vs +0.82 um on 6bba). Pairs are 85 % 6bba (106k of 125.7k), so balancing the loss 50/50 by embryo and bagging seeds reduce the convention and variance risk. Distilling toward the average of Q and the public head is a further hedge.
hypotheses.change: tools/train_coordhead.py (Vitalii's machine, where experiments/coordhead_retrain/captures lives), ~60 lines: (a) --balance embryo: per-pair loss weight so each embryo carries 50 %; (b) --ref-stems: train the x138 recipe (same code, --debias none) only on x138's 10 validator stems of the TRAINING embryo, as the out-of-embryo analogue of the public head; (c) --bag 5 seeds, with the final head distilled into one 224->32->3 net on the capture's 1 % all-peak sample plus the pairs (the kernel's make_head() fixes that architecture), target = mean of the 5 heads' bounded shifts; (d) optional --distill-public 0.5 (target = 0.5 x public + 0.5 x bag). Ship as dataset vitaliineibauer/biohub-coordhead-v2 with a v1284_head.pt in the public format. Kernel = exp56 (x138 verbatim) with ONLY the head path changed; the x138 lookup rglob('biohub-v1284-head-s075/v1284_head.pt') must be pointed at the new dataset, or the dataset folder named to match. Keep x138's knobs unchanged. Do NOT combine with any other change.

Reference REF = x138 recipe (debias none, same loss) trained on the 10 x138 validator stems of the training embryo only, i.e. out-of-embryo like the candidate. The public head is never used as the gate reference, because it is in-embryo.

hypotheses.title: Proposal-only detector copy fine-tuned on dense Ultrack/dorado labels, feeding ONLY x138's low-detection pool (readmit/gapfill)
hypotheses.mechanism: The pilkwang detector was trained with a single positive voxel per ANNOTATED nucleus and all other voxels as negatives (train_unet_transformer.py l.560-590). With 0.2-1.3 % of 44b6 annotated, unannotated neighbours are taught as background. In dense tissue that gives under-segmentation of z-blurred neighbours: in 44b6, a_never GT sit 2.3 um from an Ultrack object while our nearest node is 1.9 um from ANOTHER Ultrack object; Ultrack has +44 % interior points vs our final nodes. It also gives a neighbour-repulsion localisation bias of +0.35..+1.0 um. The loss is a density problem: the densest 6bba quartile carries 52 % of the loss. A separate detector copy fine-tuned with DENSE targets finds those nuclei. Used only as candidate peaks in x138's existing low-det pool, the candidates enter the graph only next to an open track end/start (readmit: 4 um, score >= 0.965) or on a gap line (gapfill: 3.5 um, <= 3 % added nodes). The main node set, UNet features, edge network and V1284 head stay byte-identical, so the frozen-linker failure mode (-0.038) cannot occur.
hypotheses.change: (1) Dense label builder (friend A, who holds data_external/dorado tracks.npz + kaggle44b6_in_dorado.json): for the 63 reliably registered 44b6 clips, write per-frame dense node lists = the Ultrack points inside the clip footprint, shifted by the registered offset (-0.43 um z-offset correction from r2 notes). Keep the Kaggle GT points and add the Ultrack ones; for 6bba keep the sparse GT but mask negatives farther than 7 um from any GT (positive-unlabelled masking, so unannotated 6bba nuclei are not taught as background). (2) Fine-tune a COPY of the pilkwang primary with experiments/_lib/train_patches.py: --init-weights pilkwang, --edge-loss-weight 0, 1200 it, lr 5e-5, amp, the exp03B recipe that took 27 min on 2xT4. (3) Kernel patch (tools/build_probe_kernel.py, new --patch denseprop): after the primary/secondary detection, run the copy once per frame (no TTA). Take its peaks >= 0.5 that are > 2 um from every primary peak, and append them to low_coords/low_score in the edge_cache npz (x138 cell 4 'lowdet peaks'). Add a separate readmit threshold for copy peaks, pre-registered at 0.9, and keep x138's 3 % gapfill cap.

Pass -> retrain the copy on 44b6 dense + 6bba masked, then build the kernel. If friend A's lab can replay x138's tail (h_linking-on-x138 is building it), also run the official metric on those 12 6bba videos with and without copy peaks in the pool; GATE >= +0.001 with >= 7/12 videos non-negative.

hypotheses.title: Test whether hidden annotations follow Ultrack's segmentation convention; if yes, snap/refine positions with Ultrack's public unet-simview (no training)
hypotheses.mechanism: The embryo-dependent offset (none-bias z +0.18 um on 44b6 vs +0.82 um on 6bba) is what makes any learned head risky on unseen embryos. 44b6 GT are Ultrack dorado points: 84 % within 2.5 um, GT->Ultrack median 1.29 um with no z bias, vs our nodes->GT 1.42 um. In the swap zone the nearest Ultrack point is 2.4 um from GT vs 3.7 um for our node. If the hosts (royerlab = Ultrack authors) annotated every embryo by proofreading Ultrack segments, then Ultrack's own detector (unet-simview.pt, the SimView model used for the dorado tracks) reproduces the annotation convention on ANY embryo, and a position derived from it is embryo-invariant, unlike a head trained on two embryos' clicks. The earlier snap test lost <4 um share, but it snapped to dorado points through a registration with ~0.4 um z error. Running unet-simview on the clip itself removes that confound.
hypotheses.change: Step 1 (test, no training): friend A installs ultrack and downloads unet-simview.pt (public.czbiohub.org/royerlab/ultrack/unet_weights/, reachable from his PC per CONTEXT). He runs it on 12 6bba + 12 44b6 train clips (foreground + contour maps at full resolution) and computes, for each of our pre-ILP peaks (capture coords), the foreground-weighted centroid of the Ultrack watershed basin containing the peak. Output: the train_coordhead fixed-pair table (none / public head / ultrack-centroid / 0.5-0.5 blend). Step 2 (only if the gate passes): kernel patch that runs unet-simview per frame (no TTA) and replaces the V1284 shift by the centroid shift where the basin centroid is within 2 um of the peak; ultrack wheels + weights shipped as a private dataset (no internet).

Dorado tracks were produced with unet-simview.pt (ultrack_supplementary configuration/sparse_zebrafish)
Snapping final nodes to registered Ultrack points: median GT distance 1.42 -> 1.22 um but <4 um share 0.927 -> 0.908 (registration + Ultrack noise)

It is larger only if the swap-zone advantage (2.4 vs 3.7 um) survives, which would reach the b_swap class (oracle +0.046) that de-quantisation cannot touch. That part is a guess, and unlikely.

Fail on 6bba -> the hidden-embryo convention question stays open; drop Step 2 and prefer H1's debiased head.

hypotheses.needs_user_decision: Borderline: using Ultrack's public pretrained weights on test images is inference with an external public model (allowed like any pretrained model), not matching test clips to public tracks. Confirm with the user that this fits the team policy

hypotheses.title: The 'top-team lever' as a gated long shot: joint (detector + linker) fine-tune of the primary with a corrected sparse-label loss, then recapture and retrain the head
hypotheses.mechanism: Top teams say most of their gain came from retraining the model. Our fine-tunes lost on the LB (exp33 0.944 vs 0.947), and the loss equals the node-multiplier arithmetic: +3.2 % nodes x 0.1 x 0.91 = -0.0029. B19 (recalibrate the threshold to pilkwang's node count) was dropped, never tested. Two loss changes attack the sparse-label pathology the forum describes (unannotated nuclei taught as negatives; overfit after 5-10 epochs): (i) positive-unlabelled masking (negatives only within 7 um of annotated nodes, plus hard negatives in background by intensity); (ii) a centred target convention (round instead of floor on the ds grid). Training the linker jointly, rather than freezing it, avoids the frozen-linker collapse. On x138 the head is tied to the primary's features, so the head must be recaptured and retrained on the new primary (FRIEND_A_RUN.md pipeline).
hypotheses.change: experiments/_lib/train_patches.py: add --pu-mask-um 7 and --target-round to compute_detection_loss; fine-tune the pilkwang primary jointly (edge loss on), 1200 it, lr 5e-5, amp (exp03B recipe). Pick the det threshold so the dummy-clip N_pred equals pilkwang's within +-0.5 % (B19). Recapture the V1284 head with experiments/coordhead_retrain/local_capture.py on the new primary (199 videos: friend A ~5.5 h at ~100 s/video) and retrain it with H1's recipe. Kernel = x138 with PRIMARY and head swapped.

evidence.claim: Fine-tuned primary on the TTA stack: LB 0.944 vs 0.947 (exp30/exp33); +3.2 % nodes; B19 threshold recalibration dropped untested
Sparse GT detector overfits after ~5-10 epochs: peaks/frame climb, unlabelled nuclei become negatives
Honest LOEO fine-tune 6bba -> 44b6: 0.8798 -> 0.8825 raw (+0.0027, edge -0.0015)
Plain retrains fail on LB (leonixis 0.947; Kai-Gowers 0.927 vs 0.942)
Head capture 7.2 Kaggle GPU-h for 199 videos, T4 208 s/video; 5070 Ti expected ~70-100 s/video; fine-tune 1200 it ~1 h on 5070 Ti, 27 min on Kaggle 2xT4

hypotheses.upper_bound: No mechanism-level ceiling can be derived: the in-sample lab cannot measure a primary swap (lab caveat). From the evidence: our best fine-tune was +0.0048 raw on hold12 (leaky) and +0.0027 LOEO. After removing the -0.0029 node effect, the honest upside is ~+0.003..+0.005, and it could be negative (feature shift under the retrained head).
hypotheses.expected_public_gain: -0.005..+0.004 (central -0.001; guess). Arithmetic: LOEO +0.0027 minus the risk of losing part of the head's ~+0.004 localisation value if the recaptured head is worse
hypotheses.probability: P(>= +0.005) ~0.03; P(> 0) ~0.3. Do NOT start before H1 and H2 have used friend A's GPU; run only if friend A is idle
hypotheses.validation_protocol: Two fine-tunes with the same recipe from the pilkwang init: 6bba-only -> official metric on the fixed 12 LOEO-44b6 videos, and 44b6-only -> 12 6bba videos. The references are pilkwang itself (in-sample, so conservative) and an exp03B-recipe control fine-tune on the same data (isolates the loss change). GATE: the PU/round recipe beats the control by >= +0.004 in BOTH directions at matched node count (threshold re-picked per run to N_pred = control +-0.5 %), with >= 8/12 videos non-negative. Then the recaptured head must pass H1's out-of-embryo gate on the new features. Any failure -> stop.
